Union Environment Minister and Gujarat Chief Minister inaugurate World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026 at Gandhinagar
articles.full_content:
WCEF2026 must embody spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam by developing Practical Circular Solutions for the World: CM (Gujarat), Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel Repair before Replace, Reuse before Discard, Recover before Waste - India’s Circularity Ethos rooted in Tradition: Shri Bhupender Yadav Circularity inherently Collaborative - Knowledge, Technology, Finance and Responsibility need to move across Borders and Sectors: Union Environment Minister
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav, along with Chief Minister (Gujarat), Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, inaugurated the World Circular Economy Forum 2026 at Gandhinagar today. The forum is being organised under the theme 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity', from 15th - 18th September . Other dignitaries gracing the inaugural session included Minister for Forest, Environment and Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Arjunbhai Modhwadia; Minister of State for Forests and Environment, Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Pravinbhai Mali; Ambassador of Finland to India, Ambassador of Finland to India, H.E. Mr. Mikko Kivikoski; Dy. Directoe General (Circular Economy), Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate (Netherlands), Ms. Marieke Spijkerboer; President SITRA, Mr. Atte Jääskeläinen, along with senior officials from the Government of India and Government of Gujarat.
In his special address, Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel said the first-ever hosting of WCEF in South Asia reflects India’s growing global leadership under the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He said Mission LiFE is emerging as a foundation for the global circular economy and expressed confidence that the Forum would showcase practical circular economy practices for the world.
The Chief Minister reflected on Gujarat’s journey towards environmental conservation, while maintaining a balance between development and the environment. Highlighting traditional circular practices, he cited the example of offerings at the Somnath Temple being recycled into reusable resources and generating livelihoods for local communities. He emphasised that the culture of reuse and the concept of converting waste into wealth have long been part of Indian traditions, and called for WCEF to embody the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam by developing practical circular solutions for the world.
In his keynote address on the occasion, Shri Bhupender Yadav said that for India, the circular economy is “not a new destination; it is a new way of looking at an old wisdom”. He said the principles of reuse, repair and respect for resources have been deeply embedded in India’s social and cultural fabric. “What we now describe in policy language as circularity was once simply common sense in everyday Indian life - repair before replace, reuse before discard, and recover before waste”, he stated. The Minister said the choice is not between growth and the environment, but an opportunity to make growth itself more resource-efficient, resilient

Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Monthly Bulletin August 2026
articles.full_content:
Overall LFPR increased further WPR strengthened in rural areas and stable in urban areas Rural UR recorded decline
• The overall LFPR (15+ years) increased to 55.6% in August, 2026, up from 55.4% in July, 2026.
• LFPR (15+ years and above) in rural areas stood at 58.2% in August, 2026, registering an increase of 1.2 percentage points over August 2025.
• Overall female LFPR (15+ years and above) recorded at 34.8% in August, 2026, 1.1 percentage points higher than the level recorded in August, 2025.
• Overall WPR (15+ years and above) increased to 52.8% in August 2026,the highest level recorded since March, 2026.
• Rural WPR (15+ years and above) increased by 1.3 percentage points year-on-year to 55.8% in August, 2026.
• Overall UR (15+ years and above) remained stable at 5.0% in August, 2026.
• Rural UR declined to 4.1% in August, 2026, the lowest level recorded since January 2026.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment and unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.
Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators viz. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status[1] (CWS) approach.
The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to July, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for August, 2026 is the seventeenth in the series.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
• Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) strengthened:
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above increased to 55.6% in August, 2026, from 55.4% in July, 2026. A similar trend has also been observed in rural areas, where the LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above increased to 58.2% in August, 2026, from 58.0% in July, 2026. In urban areas, LFPR remained constant at 50.4% in August, 2026 as compared to the previous month.
Compared to the corresponding month of the previous year, the overall LFPR increased by 0.6 percentage point, from 55.0% in August, 2025 to 55.6% in August, 2026. During the same period, rural LFPR also increased by 1.2 percentage points, from 57.0% to 58.2%, while urban LFPR experienced a marginal decline of 0.5 percentage point, from 50.9% to 50.4%.
Rural LFPR registered an increase of 1.2 percentage points over the corresponding month of the previous year, reaching 58.2% in August, 2026
• Female Labour Force Participation exhibits upward momentum:
The overall female LFPR experienced a moderate increase from 34.4% in July, 2026 to 34.8% in August, 2026 mainly contributed by rural female LFPR which increased to 39.4% during the current month from 38.8% recor

The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country. Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins.

Kerala’s EcoSense Scholarships: Empowering 46000 Students to Champion Waste Management
articles.full_content:
From classrooms to communities, Kerala’s EcoSense initiative is turning students into active champions of waste management under Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0. With nearly 46,000 scholarships awarded, the programme is building green skills and fostering sustainable habits among young citizens.
What if the journey towards a Garbage Free City could begin not at a waste processing facility, but inside a classroom? Kerala is doing exactly that.
Across India, the Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0 (SBM-U 2.0) is driving a new generation of initiatives that go beyond infrastructure and waste management systems to focus on people, participation and behavioural change. By engaging children and youth in practical waste-management activities, these programmes are helping make segregation, reuse, resource conservation and sustainable living a part of everyday life.
Kerala’s Student Green Brigade Scholarship – EcoSense is a powerful example of this approach. Led by the Local Self Government Department, in collaboration with the General Education Department, Kerala, the initiative is turning schools into spaces where young minds do not just learn about waste management—they actively practise it.
Implemented under the leadership of the Local Self Government Department, in collaboration with the General Education Department, Government of Kerala, EcoSense has emerged as one of the State’s largest student-focused initiatives on waste management. The programme aims to provide scholarships to 50,000 students for their active engagement in waste management while nurturing a generation equipped with green skills and a strong sense of environmental responsibility.
The scholarship programme goes beyond creating awareness. It seeks to promote scientific waste management practices, encourage students to develop innovative solutions to local waste-related challenges, reduce waste generation and build practical understanding of sustainable waste management systems.
Under the scheme, 50 students from each Grama Panchayat, 75 students from each Municipality and 100 students from each Corporation are selected for the scholarship. This year, students from Classes 6 and 7 in the Upper Primary category, Classes 8 and 9 in the High School category, and first-year students of Higher Secondary and Vocational Higher Secondary categories were included.
Each selected student receives a scholarship of ₹1,500 along with a certificate of recognition, providing both encouragement and acknowledgement of their contribution towards Swachhata.
The scale of participation reflects the growing interest among Kerala’s students in environmental action. This year, the scholarship is being distributed to 45,880 students across 986 Local Self Government Institutions. Around five lakh students from nearly 9,000 schools participated in the programme, turning the initiative into a State-wide movement of learning and action.
The programme was designed to give students hands-on exposure to waste managemen

With nearly 46,000 scholarships awarded, the programme is building green skills and fostering sustainable habits among young citizens. These nationwide surveys are pivotal in shaping national economic policies, calculating key indicators like GDP and inflation, evaluating employment trends, and assessing rural and urban socio-economic conditions.

SECL Steps Up Drive for Special Campaign 6.0, Puts E-Waste Management in Focus
articles.full_content:
Nodal Officers Deployed Across Operational Areas to Drive Cleanliness, Scrap Disposal and Sustainable Workplace Practices SECL Tops Coal Public Sector Undertakings in Scrap Disposal and Area Cleaning in Special Campaign 5.0
South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) has intensified preparations for Special Campaign 6.0, being organised under the aegis of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), with coordinated activities planned across its operational areas in Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh. The campaign will focus on cleanliness, systematic disposal of scrap, e-waste management, environmental sustainability and improved workplace practices.
To ensure effective implementation and monitoring of the campaign, SECL has appointed nodal officers across its operational areas. The officers will coordinate campaign activities, monitor progress and facilitate timely implementation of the planned initiatives.
E-waste management will be a key focus of the campaign. SECL is preparing targeted measures for the identification, segregation and systematic disposal of e-waste, along with initiatives to promote responsible waste management across its offices and operational establishments.
The preparations are being undertaken in accordance with the directions of the Ministry of Coal. During his recent field visit to SECL’s Kusmunda Mine in Korba, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Sanjiv Kumar Kassi, reviewed preparations for Special Campaign 6.0 with senior officials. He emphasised effective implementation, measurable outcomes and greater participation in the campaign.
SECL is also preparing a day-wise action plan covering cleanliness drives, identification and disposal of scrap, e-waste management, plantation activities and other initiatives aimed at creating cleaner, more sustainable and efficient workplaces.
During Special Campaign 5.0 last year, SECL ranked first among all coal Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in scrap disposal and area cleaned.
Through Special Campaign 6.0, SECL aims to further strengthen its efforts towards cleanliness, environmental responsibility, sustainable waste management and operational efficiency, with active participation of employees and other stakeholders.

The campaign will focus on cleanliness, systematic disposal of scrap, e-waste management, environmental sustainability and improved workplace practices. To ensure effective implementation and monitoring of the campaign, SECL has appointed nodal officers across its operational areas.

India to host World Circular Economy Forum 2026, themed 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity', at Gandhinagar during 15th - 18th September, 2026
articles.full_content:
Forum a Global Platform for Cross-sectoral Partnerships to facilitate Circular Finance and advancing Innovation for Circularity 2,000+ Stakeholders from 65+ Countries to participate; 125+ exhibitors to showcase Circularity Solutions at the International Expo
India would host the World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026, at Gandhinagar (Gujarat) on 15th-18th September, 2026. A First for South Asia, the forum would be jointly inaugurated on the 15th by Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, and Chief Minister of Gujarat, Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel. The forum would be organised under the theme 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity'. Other dignitaries to grace the inaugural session would include Minister for Forest, Environment and Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Arjunbhai Modhwadia; Ambassador of Finland to India, H.E. Mr. Mikko Kivikoski; Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate (Netherlands), Ms. Marieke Spijkerboer, along with senior officials from the Government of India and Government of Gujarat.
Circularity focuses on reusing, refurbishing and recycling existing materials and products and looping them back into the economy as valuable resources. Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is leading a major transformation in environmental governance, moving toward a modern circular economy. The event is being jointly organized by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) of India, the Finnish Innovation Fund Sitra, Government of Finland, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Government of India, Government of Gujarat and Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB).
The objective of WCEF 2026 is to showcase India’s initiatives for promoting circularity and enhancing international cooperation. The event would witness participation of over 2000 cross-sectoral stakeholders from 65+ countries, including business leaders, entrepreneurs , innovators, researchers, policymakers, academicians, changemakers and others. The forum will enable global collaboration and greater engagement with the Global South; facilitate mobilising of circular finance and private-sector investment; encourage policy dialogue and cross-sectoral partnerships; while advancing innovation, digitalisation and technology for circularity.
On 15th–16th September 2026, the forum would feature 4 plenaries and 16 parallel thematic sessions on application of AI, employment potential, energy production, finance, governance, sustainable products, industrial solutions, start-up ecosystem and youth leadership. Further at the event, an expo featuring 125+ national and international exhibitors would showcase practical circular solutions developed by start-ups and investment-ready innovations.
On the sidelines of WCEF, the Board of 10 Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production Patterns (10 YFP) would hold its in person meeting, on 15th September at Gandhinagar.

A First for South Asia, the forum would be jointly inaugurated on the 15th by Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, and Chief Minister of Gujarat, Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel. The forum would be organised under the theme 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity'.
